topIssues.title: [op-conductor-ops] bootstrap-cluster is not idempotent when an existing cluster has an unhealthy follower
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Netchef's generated `op-conductor-bootstrap-cluster` Job is not reliably idempotent after a conductor cluster has already been formed.

If the cluster has an elected, active leader but one or more follower sequencers are temporarily unhealthy, rerunning `op-conductor-ops bootstrap-cluster` exits 1:

```text
All sequencers are running. Bootstrapping cluster...
ERROR! Current leader is active. Please pause conductor first.
```

It exits 0 only after every sequencer happens to become healthy:

```text
All sequencers are running. Bootstrapping cluster...
All sequencers are already healthy. Skipping bootstrap.
```

This caused Netchef's bootstrap Job to retry/fail for hours on `glamsterdam-defense-2`, despite the Raft cluster already being formed and having an active leader. No conductor reset was required; the Job eventually passed when the followers caught up.

## Root cause

In `op-conductor-ops/v0.1.0`, the existing-cluster check is based on aggregate runtime health:

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/blob/op-conductor-ops/v0.1.0/op-conductor-ops/op-conductor-ops.py#L661-L675

```python
if network_obj.is_healthy() and any(
    sequencer.sequencer_active for sequencer in network_obj.sequencers
):
    typer.echo("All sequencers are already healthy. Skipping bootstrap.")
    raise typer.Exit(code=0)

leader = network_obj.find_conductor_leader()
...
if leader.conductor_active:
    print_error("Current leader is active. Please pause conductor first.")
    raise typer.Exit(code=1)
```

`Network.is_healthy()` requires every `conductor_sequencerHealthy` result to be true:

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/blob/op-conductor-ops/v0.1.0/op-conductor-ops/network.py#L42-L43

Transient follower health is not a durable indication of whether Raft membership has already been bootstrapped. Consequently, this valid state fails:

- desired Raft membership already exists
- leader is elected and active
- one sequencer is actively sequencing
- one or more followers are temporarily unhealthy/catching up

The active-leader guard is reasonable for a genuinely incomplete/destructive bootstrap. The problem is reaching it before recognizing that membership is already complete.

## Evidence

Environment:

- Network: `glamsterdam-defense-2`
- Three sequencers: `seq-0`, `seq-1`, `seq-2`
- `op-conductor-ops/v0.1.0`
- `op-conductor/v0.9.4`
- Job namespace: `ps-glamsterdam-def-2-opn-reth-f-seq-0`

Observed timeline:

```text
2026-09-02T07:33:19Z Conductors resumed. Bootstrap complete.
2026-09-02T15:24:36Z All sequencers are running. Bootstrapping cluster...
2026-09-02T15:24:36Z ERROR! Current leader is active. Please pause conductor first.
... repeated across multiple Job pods/container retries ...
2026-09-02T18:05:55Z All sequencers are running. Bootstrapping cluster...
2026-09-02T18:05:55Z All sequencers are already healthy. Skipping bootstrap.
```

Retrieve the relevant Loki records with:

```bash
gcx logs query \
  '{namespace="ps-glamsterdam-def-2-opn-reth-f-seq-0",container="op-conductor-ops"} |~ "(All sequencers are running|Current leader is active|Skipping bootstrap|Bootstrap complete|Updating cluster membership|Cluster membership updated|Conductors resumed)"' \
  --from '2026-09-02T00:00:00Z' \
  --to '2026-09-03T00:00:00Z' \
  --limit 5000 -o json \
| jq -r '
    [.data.result[] | .stream as $s | .values[] |
      [(.[0] | tonumber / 1000000000 | strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")),
       ($s.pod // ""), .[1]]]
    | sort_by(.[0])[] | @tsv
  '
```

Follower health errors during a representative failed retry:

```bash
gcx logs query \
  '{namespace=~"ps-glamsterdam-def-2-opn-reth-f-seq-[0-2]"} |~ "(Sequencer is unhealthy|server \\(follower\\) is not healthy|unsafe head is falling behind|Current leader is active)"' \
  --from '2026-09-02T17:50:00Z' \
  --to '2026-09-02T17:56:00Z' \
  --limit 5000 -o json
```

The later retries failed before calling `update_cluster_membership`; there is no evidence of membership corruption.

## Expected behavior

Once desired Raft membership exists, rerunning the generated bootstrap Job should exit successfully without requiring every follower to be healthy at that instant.

Suggested flow:

1. Wait for conductor/sequencer RPC reachability.
2. Query the leader's current Raft membership.
3. Compare stable server IDs/addresses and voting status with desired membership.
4. If membership is complete and a valid leader exists, report that the cluster is already bootstrapped and exit 0, independently of transient follower health.
5. Enter fresh/disaster-recovery bootstrap only when membership is absent or incomplete.
6. If membership is incomplete while a leader is active, fail safely with a membership-specific message rather than automatically pausing the leader.

Health may still be reported separately, but should not determine whether the cluster counts as bootstrapped.

## Impact

- Netchef deployment/health automation can remain failed while conductor itself is operational.
- Kubernetes repeatedly retries an operation that has already achieved its desired state.
- Operators receive misleading advice to pause a live conductor, which could cause an unnecessary sequencing interruption.
- Unrelated follower sync or L1 availability problems are surfaced as bootstrap failures.

topPRs.title: proxyd: send optional x-api-key header from tx validation middleware
topPRs.author: trianglesphere
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Add an optional `api_key` to `[tx_validation_middleware]`. When set, the validation client sends it on every request in the `x-api-key` header; when unset, no header is sent and behavior is unchanged.

The key is resolved through ReadFromEnvOrConfig, so it can be supplied as `$ENV_VAR` like other secrets in the config. The startup log records only whether a key is configured, never its value.

### gRPC-Go xDS servers: Denial of Service (DoS) via crash due to missing `:authority` and `Host` headers
[CVE-2026-84445](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-84445) / [GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
A vulnerability exists in gRPC-Go servers configured with `xds.NewGRPCServer()` where a crafted request missing both `:authority` and `Host` headers can cause a server panic, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

Servers built with `xds.NewGRPCServer` install an xDS routing interceptor on every RPC. This interceptor looks up the request’s `:authority` header to pick a virtual host. The HTTP/2 server transport previously accepted requests that had neither `:authority` nor `Host`. When this happened, the xDS routing interceptor attempted to access the first element of an empty slice of authorities, leading to an index out of bounds panic. Since the per-RPC goroutine does not recover from panics, the entire server process would terminate.

This panic occurs in the interceptor pipeline, meaning the transport credentials handshake (TLS, mTLS, or ALTS) and HTTP/2 connection establishment must complete successfully before the crafted request can reach this logic.
- Insecure/Standard TLS: If the server permits insecure (plaintext) connections or standard credentials (where client certs are not checked), any unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger the crash.
- mTLS / ALTS: If strict transport-level authentication is enforced at the network edge or transport layer (e.g., requiring a valid client certificate), the attacker must possess valid transport credentials to initiate the stream and trigger the panic.

##### Impact
An attacker can cause a complete outage of the gRPC server by sending a request missing both `:authority` and `Host` headers, provided they can successfully establish a transport connection.

##### Patches
The issue has been addressed in `master` (and backported to `1.83.2` and `1.82.2`). The fix updates the HTTP/2 transport layer to reject requests missing both `:authority` and `Host` headers early, maintaining consistency with and other gRPC language implementations.

#### Severity
High

### morgan vulnerable to Log Forging via unescaped Unicode line separators
[CVE-2026-15603](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15603) / [GHSA-jxfw-x594-9x9m](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-jxfw-x594-9x9m)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Morgan writes attacker-controlled request data to the access log through its tokens. The 1.11.0 fix neutralizes C0 control characters, DEL, and backslash, but it does not escape the Unicode line separators `U+0085` (NEL), `U+2028` (LINE SEPARATOR), or `U+2029` (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR). These code points are reachable through several tokens, including the request URL (`:url`), request headers such as `:user-agent` and `:referrer`, arbitrary `:req[header]` values, and the Basic auth username (`:remote-user`). NEL is valid `obs-text` in HTTP header values, so an attacker can place it in an ordinary request header.

When such a value is logged, the raw code points survive into the emitted access-log record, and downstream ECMAScript-aware or Unicode-aware log processing splits the single physical record into multiple logical records. This allows an attacker to forge log entries. The built-in `combined`, `common`, `default`, and `short` formats are affected, as well as any custom format. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-5078.

##### Patches

Users should upgrade to version 1.12.0.

##### Workarounds

None. The affected values include the request URL and request headers, which are core to access logging, so there is no practical format-based mitigation. Upgrade to 1.12.0.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 5.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N`

#### References

- [https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15603](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15603)
- [https://github.com/expressjs/morgan/commit/fbf93833186920cc39bb19b247e4a86b61bef4fe](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/morgan/commit/fbf93833186920cc39bb19b247e4a86b61bef4fe)

topPRs.title: docs: link security policy to Immunefi bounty program
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary
